title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (7-10Y nominal, $4B cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/16/2026, operation 9/17/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/18/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 7Y to 10Y, maturity range 09/18/2033 - 09/17/2036, min $0, max $4 billion. Stays estimate on the two counts the sibling treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06 entry already documented: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-16 operation announcement (preliminary CUSIP list 11:00am ET) rather than this document, checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research, promoting the proposal filed from the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 D-1 sweep. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-7y10y-2026-09-17.md. TWO CORRECTIONS THIS ENTRY OWNS, both from Treasury's own operations data (fiscaldata buybacks_operations + buybacks_security_details, 219 rows, fetched direct 2026-09-08). FIRST, CAP PARITY IS NOT PURCHASE PARITY — the proposal filed this event as the '$4B parity benchmark' proving sb0607 merely lifts the long end to the size the rest of the nominal curve already carried. True on caps, false on purchases. Across all nine operations this bucket has ever run it has filled its cap ZERO times, accepting a mean of $414 million and a median of $210 million, on a $4 billion cap since 2024-09-10; the 10Y-20Y bucket buys its entire $2 billion cap 21 times out of 21. On accepted par — the only number that reaches the market — the long end at its OLD cap already purchases four times what this bucket purchases at $4 billion, so sb0607 is the largest actual-purchase change in the nominal program rather than a normalization. SECOND, THE '7Y TO 10Y' LABEL IS WRONG ABOUT WHAT GETS BOUGHT: every eligible list in the three 2026 operations is ten 10-Year notes on the Feb/May/Aug/Nov cycle and contains no 7-Year note at all, which is mechanically necessary — a 7-Year note maturing inside 09/18/2033-09/17/2036 was issued 09/2026 or later and so is unissued or fails the first-coupon/on-the-run exclusions on operation day. The eligible COUNT is derivable rather than awaited: twelve quarterly 10-Year maturities sit in range, the newest two have not passed a first coupon, 12 - 2 = 10, matching 3 of 3 observed 2026 lists. Two cautions carried forward. sb0607 does NOT cover this bucket (it names the 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y NOMINAL sectors only), so a $4 billion print on 09-16 is the standing cap and is NOT evidence the increase took effect — that test belongs to the 09-09 announcement and the 09-10 operation. And nothing about 09-17's tape is attributable: the 10-Year TIPS auction runs 1:00pm ET forty minutes earlier, the monthly coupon announcement and housing starts share the morning, the FOMC decision landed 23.5 hours before, and opex plus the BoJ follow the next day. Estimate-labeled throughout; nothing here licenses an entry.
